summary_md:
**Thor ([@coolthor](https://x.com/coolthor/status/2115141559771390352))** reports splitting **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** across *two* DGX Sparks with TensorFold tensor parallelism (TP=2), since the weights are too large for a single box (~98 GiB per node per the attached graphic).

- Single-stream code generation came out roughly 20% ahead of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (about 111.5 vs 92.4 tok/s); single-stream Chinese was also ahead (59.2 vs 46.4 tok/s).
- With 8 concurrent Chinese streams the two models were roughly tied (~150.6 vs 148.0 tok/s), and running with PARALLEL=8 cut time-to-first-token from ~8.6 s to ~1 s.
- Thor's linked write-up on ai-muninn.com walks through the setup and the gotchas.

referenced_urls.title: [DGX Spark] DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Two DGX Sparks: TensorFold TP=2 Setup, 20% Faster Single-Stream Than Qwen3.8

relevance: A measured recipe for running a model that exceeds one Spark's memory by pairing two units, with head-to-head numbers against the Qwen3.8 Flash tier.

media.description: Hand-drawn style infographic titled 'Two Sparks, One DeepSeek V4.1 Flash' showing two cartoon DGX Spark boxes holding up a 'V4.1' crate, plus four benchmark tiles comparing against Qwen3.8.
